topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Hallmarks of Cancer Framework
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives, the multistep tumor progression model, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Sustained Proliferative Signaling and Growth Autonomy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations across extracellular sensor pathways—including Wnt, RTK, Ras-MAPK, and PI3K signaling—drive self-sufficient proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Malignancies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells evade terminal differentiation and remain in proliferative precursor states in both hematopoietic malignancies and colonic crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanisms by which disruption of p53 regulation and shifts in the Bax/BCL2 balance protect damaged cells from apoptotic death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the Hayflick limit, telomere dynamics, mechanisms of telomerase activation via TERT alterations, and the p53-dependent senescence failsafe.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming and Oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex tumor phenotypes, detailing aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring across tumor types, and the epigenetic consequences of Krebs cycle enzyme mutations.

topics.label: Induction of Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how growing tumors overcome nutrient and oxygen diffusion limits by shifting the angiogenic balance to recruit new blood vessels.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Dissemination, and Genetics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the metastatic cascade, lymphatic and vascular dissemination, seed-and-soil dynamics, and the clonal genetic landscape of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers concluding remarks on cancer heterogeneity, references recent hallmark literature, and provides housekeeping for upcoming practical sessions.
